newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels beat Hutu kids kept in container van.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels beat Hutu kids kept in container van.

text.p: Zairean rebels who abducted 52 sick Rwandan Hutu refugee children from a hospital kept them in a container van without food or water and beat some of them before releasing them five days later, U.N. agencies said on Friday.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said it had asked the Tutsi-dominated rebels, who face mounting charges of alleged human rights abuses and violence against the refugees, to explain the abduction and mistreatment.
"The children said that they were kept in a container van. Some of them were beaten. They were not fed," UNHCR spokesman Fernando del Mundo told a briefing in Geneva.
"We've raised this issue with the (rebel) authorities in Bukavu and we hope that they will respond."
Del Mundo said the rebels released the children on April 30 in the eastern town of Bukavu following a stiff U.N. protest expressing concern over their fate. They have been repatriated.

The U.N. children's agency UNICEF said the children, abducted by armed rebels from a pediatric hospital at Lwiro, some 30 kilometres (20 miles) north of Bukavu in rebel-held territory in eastern Zaire, were in a very bad shape.

UNICEF said aid agencies had verified the identity of the children returned, as well as that of 10 accompanying adults. The adults were all those abducted, contrary to a UNHCR statement on Tuesday that 60 adults were missing, it added.
Marie Heuze, a UNICEF spokeswoman, said: "They were without food and water for all these days."
"The authorities have launched an inquiry with the humanitarian agencies. We will try to shed full light."

She suggested the motivation for the kidnapping was ethnic because the children were Hutu -- Rwanda's majority tribe which led 1994's genocide of minority Tutsis now in power in Rwanda and who also forms part of the rebel force.
The war in eastern Zaire is the latest outburst of centuries-old hatred between the Hutus and the Tutsis in the troubled region.
The United States, the European Union, the United Nations and aid agencies have accused the rebels of atrocities against the Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan last week called the dispersal of refugees a policy of "slow extermination", and a U.N. food agency spokeswoman, making a comparison with Hitler's Germany, said at the time: "The expression 'Final Solution' is not exaggerated."
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide.
